correctness.rationale: The binomial series and transpose give the stated matrix and its symmetry. For u=(1-z)^{-1}-1/2 the boundary Jacobian is |u+1/2|^{-2}; it is canceled by the squared Cayley prefactor (the unweighted measures are not literally equal). Paley–Wiener then gives the normalized Laplace unitary. The atomic map sends u to tu/(1−t)+1/[2(1−t)] and the Laplace substitution gives t^{-1} exp(−x/(2t))g((1−t)x/t), hence the asserted reciprocal log-shifts and weights. For t≠1/2 the constant-coefficient symbol is 2r cos(ξL) and covers the full norm enclosure. On the normalized long translated cutoffs, each shift discrepancy has norm at most sqrt(2|L|/N); the multiplier error vanishes uniformly there, and the supports escape, giving the required singular Weyl sequence at every spectral point. Strict pointwise attenuation of both summands excludes norm attainment. At t=1/2 the doubled atom is the non-atomic multiplication model with essential range [0,4]. Strong continuity follows from dilations and dominated convergence of the locally uniformly bounded multipliers, for both terms. Testing the norm difference on unit approximate eigenvectors at the negative edge and using A_{1/2}≥0 gives the claimed lower bound. Inspected checks/finite_sections.py and frozen VERIFICATION.md; recorded finite numerical checks were not rerun and are not needed for these analytic conclusions.
